cases.name: research-spike
cases.promptMarkdown: Our bank exports can be 2 GB, with multi-line memos inside quoted fields. I'd like to switch the CLI's parsing to the vendored rowstream library in vendor/rowstream, but only if it really keeps memory under 200 MB on a file that size and gets the quoted newlines right. Its README doesn't say and nobody here has tried it. Plan it out before we write anything; assume sensible defaults rather than asking me questions.

graders.name: spike-shape
graders.evidence:
# tally plan

## Goal
Make `node src/cli.js export.csv` total a 2 GB bank export (date,amount,memo) correctly, including memos with newlines inside quoted fields, in under 200 MB peak memory, by parsing with the vendored `vendor/rowstream`. The switch only goes ahead if a spike first proves rowstream meets both bars. Done = the CLI streams the file, the total matches a known answer, and peak RSS stays under 200 MB on a 2 GB file.

## Baseline
2026-11-17 · tests: 1 pass, 0 fail · lint: none configured · build: none (Node 22.23.5, ESM)

## Now
Stage 1 of 4 · Spike: does rowstream hold 2 GB under 200 MB and parse quoted newlines?
Risk: parsing (money totals), large local temp files
Checks:
- [ ] A generated ~2 GB CSV (multi-line quoted memos, CRLF, `""` escapes, UTF-8, a `""` and a quoted newline placed on 64 KiB chunk boundaries) streams through `rows()` with peak RSS < 200 MB (proof: `/usr/bin/time -v` max RSS in the note, a test can't measure process RSS reliably)
- [ ] Row count and amount sum from `rows()` equal the generator's known values (proof: script output in the note)
- [ ] `docs/research/rowstream-spike.md` records go / no-go, numbers, run time and every parsing defect found (proof: the note)
Open: none (fallback is a default under Decisions)

## Stages
- [ ] 1. Spike: rowstream under load — throwaway generator plus harness in `$TMPDIR`, never merged; only the note is committed. Gates stages 2–4.
- [ ] 2. Tests for rowstream — it has none, so cover it before relying on it: quoted newlines, CRLF, `""` escapes, a `""` split across a chunk boundary, UTF-8 split across chunks, no trailing newline, empty fields. Fix defects in the vendored copy and note the fixes in its README.
- [ ] 3. Stream the CLI — replace `readFileSync`/`split` with `rows()`, find the amount column by its header name, add cents into a running total (never build an array of rows), and fail with the row number on a non-numeric amount. Tests over fixture files run the CLI end to end.
- [ ] 4. Memory check you can rerun — commit `scripts/bench-memory.js` (generates a file of a given size, runs the CLI, asserts peak RSS < 200 MB and the expected total). Kept out of `npm test` because of the 2 GB file. Run it at 2 GB.

## Decisions
- 2026-11-17 · The switch depends on the spike: if stage 1 fails either bar, stop and bring the numbers to the user before stages 2–4 — the user asked for proof before adopting it.
- 2026-11-17 · If the spike fails because of a small, local defect (e.g. a chunk-boundary bug), the default is to fix it in the vendored copy instead of dropping rowstream; anything structural goes back to the user. Rowstream is ours to patch: it is vendored from an internal tool, and nobody upstream maintains it.
- 2026-11-17 · Synthetic data only; no real bank exports in the repo or in tests — they contain personal financial data.
- 2026-11-17 · The CLI sums as it streams instead of collecting rows — an array of millions of row objects would break the 200 MB limit no matter which parser reads the file.
- 2026-11-17 · The amount column is found by its header name (`amount`), and the first row is treated as the header, as today. A missing column or a non-numeric amount exits non-zero with the row number — today a bad amount silently becomes NaN, which is wrong for money.
- 2026-11-17 · Only peak memory has a limit. Run time is recorded in the spike note but is not a pass/fail bar, because the user set none.

## Open questions
- Is a quoted memo with a lone `"` inside it (e.g. `ab"c`) valid in the bank's exports? rowstream toggles quoting on any `"`. The default is to treat it as malformed, like RFC 4180 does. User decides; it affects stage 2 tests only.
